deep.reconstruction:
Context: a station adjustment for Varel in Gauss's Hanoverian triangulation (Gradmessung), probably c. 1824–25, although the bundle is labelled 1813. The previous page (Bremerlehe) and next page (Langwarden) carry out the same kind of computation for neighbouring stations.

(1) Provisional directions. Six target directions are given, each with an unknown correction:
- 1 Jever Heliotrop: 142°58'8.166" + a
- 2 Jever Thurm: 142°58'57.084" + b
- 3 Langwarden: 207°44'2.052" + c (with a side note +6.674", probably a centring or reduction value)
- 4 Bremerlehe: 239°21'4.048" + d
- 5 Golzwarden: 284°22'15.211" + e
- 6 Garlste: 292°10'11.150" + f

(2) Observation equations. Eleven measured angles i.j are listed. Each carries a weight p, the number of repetitions, sometimes split into two series (e.g. 96 = 56 + 40). For each, Gauss writes the residual as computed minus observed:
  v_ij = (D_j − D_i − M_ij) + (x_j − x_i).
Example: 1.2 gives 57.084 − 8.166 − 49.222 = −0.304, so v = −0.304 − a + b. All eleven constants recompute exactly.

(3) Normal equations. Minimising Σ p v² gives, for each unknown x_k, Σ p v ∂v/∂x_k = 0. The diagonal entries are the summed weights of the angles at each direction: 205, 42, 195, 195, 34, 151. Each off-diagonal entry is −p for the angle joining the two directions. The constants are Σ ±p·(const).
- Every row sums to zero, so the matrix is singular. This is the undetermined common orientation; the solution is fixed only up to an additive constant.
- Recomputed constants: +0.001, −0.003, −0.007, 0.000, −0.014, +0.023. They are essentially zero, so the provisional directions were already the least-squares solution of these 11 angles.

(4) Previously excluded observations. Four further series had not been used ('Hiebei waren nicht zugezogen'):
- 1.3 (p = 11): 64°45'54.182"
- 3.4 (p = 20): 31°37'2.912"
- 3.6 (p = 12): 84°26'12.354"
- 4.6 (p = 35): 52°49'7.664"
Their residuals against the provisional directions are −0.296, −0.916, −3.256, −0.562; all four check.

(5) Admitting them. Including them changes the directions by a = −0.241, b = −0.127, c = −0.342, d = −0.123, e = +0.005, f = +0.123. The new table is: 7.925, 56.957, 1.710, 3.925, 15.216, 11.273 (seconds in each case).

(6) Merged angles. Each pair of series is combined as a weighted mean (all four check):
- 1.3: (96·53.401 + 11·54.182)/107 = 53.481
- 3.4: (49·1.429 + 20·2.912)/69 = 1.859
- 3.6: (44·8.778 + 12·12.354)/56 = 9.544
- 4.6: (69·7.312 + 35·7.664)/104 = 7.430

(7) Second pass. New residuals are computed with the new directions, and new normal equations are formed. Diagonals are 216, 42, 238, 250, 34, 198; constants are −0.032, −0.004, +0.114, −0.095, +0.014, +0.003. The constants sum to 0, and all recompute from the listed residuals. Divided by the diagonals, they imply further corrections of only about 0.0005", so the solution is confirmed to accuracy.

(8) Side list. Unadjusted directions to Sandstedt, Neuenkirchen, Rastede and Westerstede are noted for use elsewhere.
errors: Second tableau, angle 1.2: from the new directions, 56.957 − 7.925 − 49.222 = −0.190, not −0.187 as written. The same follows from the first pass: −0.304 + 0.241 − 0.127 = −0.190. This 0.003" slip carries into the a- and b-constants of the second normal equations, but is negligible.
First normal equations: the signs of the b- and e-constants are obscured in the manuscript. Recomputation gives −0.003 (b) and −0.014 (e), so both should be negative.
The struck note '+0,675 6.6' and '−1"947' beside the excluded 4.6 line are unclear in meaning. They may be a trial residual or reduction; this cannot be verified.

results.what: Station adjustment of horizontal directions from weighted repeated angle measurements, by least squares: observation equations, normal equations (singular because orientation is free), solution, and recomputed residuals
results.modern_name: Least-squares station adjustment (direction/angle adjustment) via normal equations
results.usually_credited_to: Gauss (least squares 1795/1809; geodetic station adjustment as in the Hanover triangulation and the Supplementum theoriae combinationis, 1826/28); later systematised by Bessel and Gerling

results.what: Weighted mean of two series of the same angle, with weights equal to repetition counts
Re-adjustment after admitting previously excluded observations, with the normal-equation constants checked to vanish
results.modern_name: Sequential/iterative refinement of a least-squares solution

deep.surprise_reason: This is a routine geodetic station adjustment from Gauss's Hanover triangulation. The least-squares method, and his use of it in exactly this form, are well documented. It is of archival interest only, for the specific Varel data.

checkable.asserts: First normal equation constant for a = +0.001
First normal equation constant for b = -0.003 (sign obscured in MS)
First normal equation constant for e = -0.014
First normal equation constant for f = +0.023
Second normal equation constant for c = +0.114
First normal matrix has zero row sums (singular: orientation free)

In the second normal equations' b-row, the c-column entry is erased/blank (should be '.'), consistent with no 2.3 angle.
